headline: The United States has a distribution, timing, quality, infrastructure, and governance problem as much as a national-volume problem; irrigation dominates consumptive use, while urban and industrial risks are intensely local.
key_findings: The latest fully comparable all-category inventory is 2015: 281 Bgal/d freshwater withdrawal out of 322 Bgal/d total.
For modeled 2010–20 covered sectors, irrigation consumed 75.698 Bgal/d versus 4.219 for public supply and 2.904 for freshwater thermoelectric power.
Nearly 27 million people lived in watersheds where demand approached or exceeded modeled natural supply during 2009–20.

The most urgent horizons begin now: current watershed stress and drought restrictions; Colorado River rule changes in 2027; Texas/New Mexico supply gaps and project needs in the 2030s onward; agricultural groundwater transitions continuing through 2100.
Coastal freshwater loss is not governed by sea level alone. Pumping, canals, drought, recharge, well design, and geology determine whether and when individual wellfields become saline.
Miami-Dade is vulnerable, but the cited model does not support a claim of wellfield failure through 2040; Long Island and Brunswick show why localized current impacts still matter.
Direct data-center water was about 47.8 Mgal/d nationally in 2023 and is projected at about 101–203 Mgal/d in 2028; national percentages are small, local siting effects can be large.
Manufacturing withdrawals are incompletely measured and plastics cannot yet be assigned a credible national water total or ban-savings coefficient.

Desalination is viable for selected municipal increments and brackish sources, but replacing all 2015 domestic use would imply roughly 532 Carlsbad-size capacity equivalents and 118–165 TWh/year before several additional burdens.
Atmospheric water generators can support drinking/emergency niches; current output, energy, climate dependence, and water-quality requirements make whole-house or community-base supply implausible.
priority_dashboard_messages: Show withdrawal and consumptive use side by side.
Map dependence and failure pathways, not unsupported 'runs out by' dates.
Connect every future year to its evidence type and assumptions.
Make local seasonal stress the denominator for new facilities.
Treat water quality and infrastructure outages as availability failures.
Compare interventions as portfolios with energy, brine, ecosystem, cost, time, and equity.
near_term_research_priority: Build facility- and watershed-resolved plastics and data-center water inventories, then integrate them with NWAA supply-demand layers and utility source portfolios.
